title: The daemon resolves host context for human migration reverts
description: Fourth producer child of task-78eedd8ebc2b43c581ac21ea28648a9a (logical producer2), governor-directed re-slice19:10Z. At local0737 and ownerorigin4253, no non-test migrateDown: configuration exists. async-entries.ts139/322 spreads optional options.migrateDown; migrate-down-command.ts139–146 refuses MIGRATE_DOWN_UNCONFIGURED without host databaseUrl/workspace/projectRoot. Command537 and real revert engine are DONE; DO NOT republish kind/rebuild revert. Forward sibling2db owns reusable per-project/environment host-context resolver; depend on it instead of creating a second secret-resolution policy. Resolve request environment freshly, not one daemon-wide static URL incorrectly reused for every environment. Preserve default unconfigured refusal where evidence absent. Parent78 is browser/live proof consumer.
definitionOfDone: Default production daemon composition provides existing migrate-down command with host-resolved projectRoot/workspace and database context for exactly the admitted request environment. Test actual dispatch through default composition, not an isolated entry constructed with hardcoded databaseUrl; two environments prove isolation.

Unconfigured/missing/unreadable host context refuses MIGRATE_DOWN_UNCONFIGURED or the existing precise environment resolver code at its real layer before engine reads or writes. No fallback to arbitrary inherited DATABASE_URL, no browser-supplied URL/root/workspace, no secret-containing diagnostic.

Preserve HUMAN/operator-only async fence, HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS and MCP exclusion. Unauthorized real dispatch is rejected with code+layer before resolver/decrypt/engine effects; no new roster entries or authority widening. Authorized path reaches existing revertLastBatch and names the APPLIED request batch.

Live disposable-PostgreSQL arm through production composition applies two batches via shipped forward edge, reverts named last batch, asserts earlier schema remains and reverted schema disappears, then reads REVERTED receipt. Backup failure/not-last-batch/replay/concurrent revert preserve engine guarantees and unchanged schema where refused; no automatic restore.

Teardown every process/container/temp tree in finally on all outcomes; no connection value, SQL, password, derived credential value or tool banner in log/evidence. Fresh focused daemon tests/typecheck and named broader gates have nonzero counts; parent78 consumes wiring. Physical .js bridges for new runtime entrypoints.
taskRails: Reuse sibling2db host context and existing revert engine/fence. Production database values never enter browser or durable payload.
Do not overwrite whole shared registry files. Coordinate explicit paths and re-read owner-origin changes after reconciliation.

implementationPlan.description:
**MEASURE FIRST, NO EDITS.** Two directions, because this row's description makes claims in both (global rail 6). Record each command and its output in the step note.

(a) THE GAP IS REAL: `git grep -n "migrateDown" -- apps/daemon/src` minus tests returns only the type at `daemon-command-async-entries.ts:140-141` and the spread at `:305`; `daemon-command-registry.ts:294` does not pass it; `DaemonCommandRegistryOptions` carries no projectRoot/workspace/database context. Production migrate_down has always refused UNCONFIGURED.

(b) THE MECHANISM: quote `migrate-down-command.ts:93-98`. `identity` (carrying the request environment) is computed at :93; the three host values are read from the CLOSURE at :94-95. Confirm `createMigrateDownCommandHandler` is invoked once at composition, so those are construction-time statics and no value of them can satisfy DoD 1's two-environment isolation.

(c) **WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT** — the direction that stops a rebuild: `migrate-down-real.test.ts` already drives live PostgreSQL through the REGISTERED command, applies two batches via real `migrateWithBackup`, reverts the last, asserts batch one survives and reads the receipt. Record what it covers and that `:138` hardcodes `databaseUrl: url` — the one thing DoD 1 forbids as evidence.

(d) THE SIBLING SEAM IS ABSENT: `git grep "hostContext\|resolveHostContext\|HostContext" -- apps/daemon/src packages` minus tests returns ZERO. Re-run it: if `task-2db55fca` has landed a resolver by the time you start, read its EXPORTED signature and confirm it is keyed by ENVIRONMENT NAME. **If it is keyed by `LaunchPurpose`, STOP and report** — `PURPOSE_ENVIRONMENTS[purpose]` cannot express an arbitrary admitted request environment, and adapting around it means writing the second secret-resolution policy rail 1 forbids.

**THE SEAM: HOST CONTEXT BECOMES PER-REQUEST.** `apps/daemon/src/deployment/migrate-down-command.ts`.

(a) Export a type beside the options it belongs to — `MigrateDownHostContext` = `{ databaseUrl, projectRoot, workspace }`, all required strings.

(b) On `MigrateDownCommandOptions` (:23-32) REPLACE the three optional strings with one optional resolver: `readonly hostContext?: (environment: string) => MigrateDownHostContext | null`. Keeping the strings alongside it would leave two ways to configure the same thing and a silent precedence question.

(c) At :94-98, call it with `identity.environment` — already in scope from :93 — and keep the refusal EXACTLY as it is today when the resolver is absent, returns null, or returns any empty field: `MIGRATE_DOWN_UNCONFIGURED` at `DAEMON_COMMAND_SEAM`, status 422, BEFORE any engine read or write. The per-field message (`no database/workspace/project root is configured on this daemon`) names the FIELD and never the value — preserve that exactly; a resolved database URL must never reach a refusal string (epic rail 3).

(d) The async-entries comment at :137-139 already states that ABSENT is a refusing state, never a skipped one. That contract is PRESERVED, not re-litigated — say so in a comment at the resolver call so the next reader does not read the new indirection as a new fallback.

NO NEW MODULE and therefore no new `.js` bridge: the type lives here, the implementation is `task-2db55fca`'s. Say that explicitly in the step note so DoD 5's bridge clause is answered rather than left open.

**THREAD IT THROUGH THE PRODUCTION COMPOSITION.** Two shared registry files — rail 2 applies: edit the explicit lines, never regenerate, and RE-READ both immediately before writing, because owner-origin reconciliation has moved them before.

(a) `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-async-entries.ts:140-141`: change `migrateDown?: Pick<MigrateDownCommandOptions, "clock" | "databaseUrl" | "ports" | "projectRoot" | "workspace">` to pick `"clock" | "hostContext" | "ports"`. Leave the `:305` spread shape alone — it already forwards whatever the option carries.

(b) `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts`: add `readonly migrateDown?: …` to `DaemonCommandRegistryOptions` (the block at :107-164) and add the conditional spread to the `createAsyncCommandEntries({…})` call at :294, in the SAME `...(options.X === undefined ? {} : { X: options.X })` form as the eight seams already there. Do not invent a different shape for the ninth.

(c) DO NOT widen authority. No new roster entry, no capability change. `DEPLOYMENT_MIGRATE_DOWN_COMMAND_KIND` keeps `requiredCapability: CAPABILITIES.GOAL` and the operator fence at the handler's entry (`migrate-down-command.ts:88-91`, `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED @ DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION`, 403). `agentCapabilitiesFor` answers null for it, so no seat is ever granted it — leave that alone.

**MOVE THE SHARED HARNESS, KEEP BOTH TABLES HONEST.** `apps/daemon/src/deployment/migrate-down-test-fixtures.ts`.

(a) `:180-183` currently assigns `migrateDown: { clock, databaseUrl: DATABASE_URL, ports, projectRoot: root, workspace: root }`. Convert to the resolver form: `hostContext: (environment) => …`. Have it answer for a NAMED environment and answer `null` for any other — not a constant-returning function. A resolver that ignores its argument makes every isolation arm in step 5 vacuous, and that is exactly the class of test this row exists to replace.

(b) `:186-188`, the `unconfigured` table, passes NO `migrateDown` at all — an unconfigured daemon, not a mocked one, as its own comment says. It must keep refusing for the same reason and by the same code. Do not give it a resolver that returns null; the ABSENT case and the NULL case are two distinct arms and step 5 asserts both.

(c) `migrate-down-journey.test.ts` consumes this harness and names none of the three fields itself — confirm that by grep before you edit, and if it does name them, STOP and report rather than adding a sixth file to this row (global rail 19).

**THE ARMS — ISOLATION, REFUSAL, AUTHORITY, SECRECY.** `apps/daemon/src/deployment/migrate-down-real.test.ts`, driven through the DEFAULT composition, never an isolated entry with a hardcoded databaseUrl (DoD 1 names that exclusion explicitly, and `:138` is the line that currently does it).

(a) **TWO ENVIRONMENTS PROVE ISOLATION** (DoD 1). Dispatch a real migrate_down naming environment A and assert the revert reached A's database and workspace; dispatch naming environment B and assert it reached B's. Assert the resolver was CALLED WITH the admitted environment — an arm where both environments resolve to the same host would pass while the defect stands.

(b) **THREE REFUSAL ARMS** (DoD 2), each asserting the specific code AND the layer that answered, and each asserting the schema is UNCHANGED afterwards: resolver ABSENT; resolver returns NULL for the named environment; resolver returns a record with an empty field. All three are `MIGRATE_DOWN_UNCONFIGURED @ DAEMON_COMMAND_SEAM`, 422, raised before any engine read or write. Asserting only 'refused' is one added layer away from vacuous (global rail 1).

(c) **AUTHORITY UNCHANGED** (DoD 3). A non-operator principal is rejected with `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED @ DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION`, 403, BEFORE the resolver is consulted — assert the resolver was NOT called, so no resolution or decryption happens for an unauthorised caller. The authorised path reaches the existing `revertLastBatch` and names the APPLIED request batch.

(d) **NO SECRET ON ANY PATH** (epic rail 3, DoD 5). Over the CONFIGURED, successful path, assert the resolved database URL, its password and any derived credential appear in NO log line, NO durable payload, NO receipt and NO refusal message. Assert this positively against captured output, not by reading the source.

(e) **TEARDOWN ON EVERY EXIT PATH** (epic rail 4), refusing arms included: every container, process and temp tree released in `finally`, on success and on failure alike. Keep the existing `MOE_MIGRATION_RESTORE=1` opt-in and its fail-rather-than-skip behaviour — do not add a second flag or a silent skip.

REUSE the existing two-batch live journey. Do NOT rebuild it.

**MUTATION DRILL, GATES, SELF-REVIEW.** Load `adversarial-self-review` first.

**(a) RESTORE RULE, before any mutation** (global rail 13). `git status --porcelain` every path you will mutate and RECORD the output — peer paths are dirty in this shared checkout; note them, never revert or stash them, and never treat them as a stop condition. Back EVERY path up OUT OF TREE (%TEMP%, suffixed with your worker id). Restore FROM THE BACKUP — never `git checkout --` or `git restore`. Prove the restore by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore: a PowerShell copy can silently no-op and 'the command returned' is not evidence the bytes moved. An empty `git diff` on a path you know you mutated is a RED FLAG, not reassurance.

**(b) TWO DRILLS, each quoted with its failing line.**
  1. Make the resolver ignore its argument and return one host context for every environment — the pre-fix behaviour. Step 5(a) must go RED. This is the whole point of the row; if it stays green the isolation arm is vacuous.
  2. Move the resolver call AFTER the engine read. Step 5(b) must go RED on 'schema unchanged'. This proves the refusal really precedes every effect rather than merely returning first.

**(c) GATES (DoD 5).** RECORDED verification is the scoped owned command actually run, exit 0, with its `Test Files N passed` count line and every filter and env flag INSIDE the recorded string — an exit-0 leg with no count line ran NOTHING, and `pnpm --filter <pkg>` prints 'No projects matched' and exits 0 for a package that does not exist. DISCLOSE `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm typecheck` with exit codes, failing-file sets and the `(AFTER − BEFORE) ∩ owned = ∅` computation against the merge base. Root `pnpm test` covers no `apps/**` file — say that rather than quoting a bare root count line. State plainly whether the live arm ran with `MOE_MIGRATION_RESTORE=1` or did not, and which lanes you did not run.

**(d) SELF-REVIEW.** Can any path reach an inherited `DATABASE_URL`? Can a browser-supplied URL, root or workspace reach the resolver? Does an unauthorised caller cause any resolution or decryption? Is any container or temp tree still alive after a REFUSED arm? Does the refusal message still name only the field? Would you be embarrassed if this shipped?

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
CHOSEN: replace the three optional strings on `MigrateDownCommandOptions` with ONE optional per-request resolver, `(environment: string) => MigrateDownHostContext | null`, called with `identity.environment` at the existing :94 site. Absent resolver, or a null answer, keeps the EXISTING `MIGRATE_DOWN_UNCONFIGURED @ DAEMON_COMMAND_SEAM` refusal byte-identically — the async-entries comment at :137-139 already documents absence as a refusing state and that contract is preserved, not re-litigated.

REJECTED: keep the three strings and add an environment-keyed record (`Record<string, {databaseUrl, …}>`). It puts the environment roster in the composition instead of the resolver, so every new environment edits the daemon wiring, and it forces the whole map to be materialised — including secrets for environments the request never named. A function resolves exactly the admitted environment and nothing else.

REJECTED: resolve inside `createMigrateDownCommandHandler` by reaching for an environment store handle. That builds a SECOND secret-resolution policy, which the row's description and rail 1 forbid, and it makes the command untestable without a store.

REJECTED: reuse `launchDelivery(config, purpose)`. Its header (environment-launch-resolver.ts:172-180) says a REFUSAL becomes `undefined` — the refusal-to-undefined convenience 2db's own description warns against for required DB context. A migrate_down that cannot distinguish 'withheld' from 'could not read' would refuse UNCONFIGURED for an unreadable store and hide a real fault.

NO NEW RUNTIME MODULE, therefore NO NEW `.js` BRIDGE. The resolver TYPE lives in `migrate-down-command.ts` beside the options it belongs to; the implementation is 2db's. DoD 5's bridge clause is satisfied vacuously and the step note must say so rather than leaving a grader to wonder.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
RE-MEASURED AT HEAD, BOTH DIRECTIONS (global rail 6). The row's diagnosis holds and I found the exact mechanism; I also found that a large part of DoD 4 is ALREADY BUILT and must not be rebuilt.

THE DEFECT, PRECISELY. `migrate-down-command.ts:93-99`:
```
const identity = migrationCommandIdentity(input, projectId);          // :93  carries the REQUEST environment
const databaseUrl = options.databaseUrl ?? "", workspace = options.workspace ?? "";  // :94  CLOSURE constants
const projectRoot = options.projectRoot ?? "";                        // :95
if (databaseUrl.length === 0 || workspace.length === 0 || projectRoot.length === 0) {
  throw new DomainRefusal(MIGRATE_DOWN_UNCONFIGURED, DAEMON_COMMAND_SEAM, …, 422);  // :96-98
}
```
`createMigrateDownCommandHandler` is called ONCE at composition (`daemon-command-async-entries.ts:305`), so those three values are CONSTRUCTION-TIME STATICS. `identity.environment` is per-request. A daemon configured with one databaseUrl applies it to EVERY environment — verbatim the failure the description names ('one daemon-wide static URL incorrectly reused for every environment'). Filling the existing option in with values CANNOT satisfy DoD 1; the option's SHAPE is the defect.

THE ORDER IS ALREADY FAVOURABLE: `identity` is computed at :93, BEFORE the config read at :94, so `identity.environment` is in scope at the refusal site. The change is surgical, not a restructure.

NO PRODUCTION COMPOSITION SUPPLIES IT. `git grep migrateDown -- apps/daemon/src` minus tests returns only the type at async-entries.ts:140-141 and the spread at :305. The only assignments are `migrate-down-test-fixtures.ts:180` and `migrate-down-real.test.ts:138`. `daemon-command-registry.ts:294` spreads eight optional seams into `createAsyncCommandEntries` and `migrateDown` is not among them, and `DaemonCommandRegistryOptions` (:107-164) carries no projectRoot, no general workspace and no environment store config — only `environmentCredential` (:127) and `previewWorkspace` (:154). So production migrate_down has ALWAYS refused MIGRATE_DOWN_UNCONFIGURED. Confirms the description.

MOST OF DoD 4 ALREADY EXISTS — DO NOT REBUILD IT. `migrate-down-real.test.ts` already drives a live PostgreSQL through the REGISTERED command via `createAsyncCommandEntries`, applies TWO batches through the real `migrateWithBackup`, reverts the last, asserts batch one survives, reads the receipt, and is opt-in behind `MOE_MIGRATION_RESTORE=1` (failing rather than skipping when the flag is set and Docker is absent). `migrate-down-test-fixtures.ts:43` states the only doubles are the two host ports. What that file LACKS is exactly what this row owes: `:138` constructs the entry with a hardcoded `databaseUrl: url`, which DoD 1 explicitly forbids as evidence. The work is to make it RESOLVE, and to add the second environment.

THE SIBLING SEAM. No host-context resolver exists anywhere: `git grep 'hostContext|resolveHostContext|HostContext' -- apps/daemon/src packages` minus tests returns ZERO. `task-2db55fca` is in PLANNING right now and its own DoD says only that a resolver composed there MAY be reused — its existence and shape are not yet fixed. THIS ROW OWNS THE SEAM SHAPE; 2db OWNS THE IMPLEMENTATION. I posted the binding constraint to #architects for architect-aa54e231: the resolver must be keyed by ENVIRONMENT NAME, because the shipped `resolveEnvironmentLaunch(config, purpose)` (environment-launch-resolver.ts:133) takes a `LaunchPurpose` and derives the environment through `PURPOSE_ENVIRONMENTS[purpose]`, which cannot express an arbitrary admitted request environment.
planningNotes.risks:
1. THE SEAM MUST BE KEYED BY ENVIRONMENT NAME. If task-2db55fca ships a `LaunchPurpose`-keyed resolver, this row cannot consume it and the dependency is dead. Constraint posted to architect-aa54e231 while 2db is still in PLANNING. If 2db lands purpose-keyed anyway, STOP and report rather than adapting around it — adapting means writing the second secret-resolution policy rail 1 forbids.

2. DO NOT REBUILD THE LIVE ARM. `migrate-down-real.test.ts` already does the disposable-PostgreSQL, two-batch, revert-the-last, batch-one-survives journey through the registered command. This row makes it RESOLVE instead of hardcode and adds the second environment. Rebuilding it would duplicate a live-Docker gate and breach epic rail 4's teardown discipline twice over.

3. THE REFUSAL MUST NOT MOVE. `MIGRATE_DOWN_UNCONFIGURED @ DAEMON_COMMAND_SEAM`, status 422, still fires BEFORE any engine read or write, and its per-field message (`no database/workspace/project root is configured on this daemon`) is existing behaviour. Assert the CODE AND THE LAYER, and that the schema is untouched — a test asserting only 'refused' is one added layer away from vacuous (global rail 1).

4. NO SECRET ANYWHERE (epic rail 3). The resolved databaseUrl must not reach a log line, a durable payload, a receipt, a refusal message or a test fixture committed to the tree. The existing refusal message names the FIELD, never the value — keep it that way. Assert the absence positively over the configured path, not by reading the code.

5. `migrate-down-test-fixtures.ts` is the SHARED harness for both the configured and the unconfigured tables (`:170` and `:186`). Changing the option shape moves both; the `unconfigured` table at :186-188 passes NO migrateDown at all and must keep refusing for the same reason it does today.

6. TEARDOWN ON EVERY EXIT PATH (epic rail 4), including the refusing arms. A test that leaks a container or a temp tree makes every later gate on this board inadmissible.

7. `daemon-command-registry.ts` is a shared registry file. Rail 2: edit the explicit lines, never regenerate the file, and re-read it before writing — owner-origin reconciliation has moved it before.
